Why the ferry timetable changed

STORY-MARKER The island ferry moved its first sailing forty minutes earlier this spring, and the harbour office says the change was driven by the tide tables rather than by any complaint from passengers or crew.

Low water now falls closer to dawn for most of the summer, which leaves the old departure time stranded on a ramp that the heavier vessel cannot safely use without scraping its hull on the concrete.

The office tried shifting only the busiest days, but the split schedule confused regular commuters so badly that the simpler answer was to move every weekday sailing and print one clear timetable.

Commuters who relied on the later boat have been offered a connecting bus from the mainland terminal, and the harbour office will review the arrangement again once the autumn tides return to normal.

MORE-MARKER More from the harbour: the lifeboat crew raised enough money this year to replace the old launch winch, and the volunteers who organised the raffle say next year they will aim even higher.

Also this week: the fish market is trialling a Saturday evening opening through August, and traders say early numbers suggest visitors are happy to shop later once the day boats have landed.

COMMENT-MARKER I take the early ferry every morning and honestly the new time is better for me, because I used to wait an hour on the mainland before my shift started at the depot.
